title: George Boole
name: George Boole
summary: English mathematician whose algebra of logic became a central mathematical foundation for digital circuits and computation.
whyThisMatters: Boolean algebra supplied a practical language for reasoning about binary states. It later became indispensable for switching theory, programming, and the design of systems that enforce and evaluate security decisions.

sections.overview:
George Boole developed an algebraic treatment of logical propositions. His 1854 book An Investigation of the Laws of Thought presented the work now known as Boolean algebra.

Lasting technical influence

The later connection between Boolean logic and electrical switching made the work central to digital computing. Modern software, hardware, and security-policy logic all depend on related binary operations.

In memoriam

Boole died in 1864. His ideas outlived the technology of his era and became part of computing’s basic vocabulary.
